hints: Notice where each original force acts: the $3\text{ N}$ force is at the top rim pointing up and the $4\text{ N}$ force is at the centre pointing right.
Check the moment of each force about the centre of the disc and add them to find the total turning effect.
Combine $3\text{ N}$ up and $4\text{ N}$ right by Pythagoras to get magnitude and direction, then require the single force to give the same moment about the centre.
walkthrough: Find the resultant magnitude from the perpendicular components: $F = \sqrt{(3\text{ N})^2 + (4\text{ N})^2} = 5\text{ N}$ directed up and to the right.
Calculate the total moment about the disc centre. The $3\text{ N}$ line passes vertically through the centre, so its perpendicular distance is zero.
The $4\text{ N}$ line passes horizontally through the centre, so its perpendicular distance is also zero. Total moment about the centre is therefore zero.
A single equivalent force must also have zero moment about the centre, so its line of action must pass exactly through the centre dot.
Only a $5\text{ N}$ arrow from the centre pointing north-east has the correct magnitude, direction and zero-moment line. This is option A.

options.A: The $5\text{ N}$ arrow acts through the centre in the $3\text{ N}$ up and $4\text{ N}$ right direction, giving zero moment about the centre like the original forces.
options.B: The $5\text{ N}$ line is shifted above the centre, so it would exert a moment about the centre which the original two forces do not.
options.C: Although direction is correct, the line is displaced from the centre so its moment about the centre is not zero.
options.D: The $5\text{ N}$ line starts away from the centre, so it would produce a non-zero moment about the centre.
